extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent practitioners, applicants and their attorneys/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on proper procedures and substantive requirements for amending patent applications and patents (claims, drawings, specification), and on use and sufficiency of affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 to antedate references and overcome prior-art rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the original patent drawings are not permitted. Any change to the patent drawings must be by way of a new sheet of drawings with the amended figures identified as “amended” and with added figures identified as “new” for each sheet changed submitted in compliance with § 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a change to the drawings is desired, a sketch in permanent ink showing proposed changes in red, to become part of the record, must be filed for approval by the examiner and should be in a separate paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend disclosure to correct inaccuracies
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue enlargement time limit and new matter prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No reissue patent shall be granted enlarging the scope of the claims of the original patent unless applied for within two years from the grant of the original patent, pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 251. No amendment to the patent may introduce new matter or be made in an expired patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments reference basis for reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments must be made relative to the patent specification, including the claims, and drawings, which is in effect as of the date of filing of the reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the description and claims in patents involved in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with § 1.530(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'brackets' in claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'brackets' set forth in 37 CFR 1.121(a) means square brackets, thus: [ ]. It does not encompass and is to be distinguished from parentheses ().
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment using parentheses to indicate canceled matter in a claim rewritten under 37 CFR 1.121(a) may be held not fully responsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim rewritten to independent form
rubrics_metrics.description: Where, by amendment under 37 CFR 1.121(a), a dependent claim is rewritten to be in independent form, the subject matter from the prior independent claim should be considered to be 'added' matter and should be underlined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact instructions for insertions/deletions (37 CFR 1.121)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim may be amended by specifying only the exact matter to be deleted or inserted by an amendment and the precise point where the deletion or insertion is to be made, where the changes are limited to deletions and/or the addition of no more than five (5) words in any one claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than five words are added in at least one claim the amendment will not be entered; applicant is given one month (30 days) to supply an amendment in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 (extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) may be granted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim cancellation or rewriting format (37 CFR 1.121(a)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim may be amended by directions to cancel the claim or by rewriting such claim with underlining below the matter added and brackets around the matter deleted. The rewriting of a claim in this form will be construed as directing the deletion of the previous version of that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a previously rewritten claim is again rewritten, underlining and bracketing will be applied relative to the previous version, with parenthetical expression 'twice amended,' 'three times amended,' etc., following the original claim number. No interlineations or deletions of any prior amendment may appear in the currently submitted version. A claim canceled by amendment can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification when brackets/underlining use is unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant's use of brackets or underlining makes it unclear whether certain matter is intended to appear in the issued patent, applicant must clearly indicate intention in reply to the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is given one month (30 days) to supply an amendment in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 and the notice to avoid abandonment (extensions may be granted). Examiner should attempt telephone clarification before sending the Office action; substance of interview must be made of record. Form paragraph restarting time period should not be used in reissue or reexamination applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments — defective directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Directions for the entry of an amendment may be defective (e.g., inaccuracy in the line designated or lack of precision where the word occurs more than once in the specified line). If it is clear from context what is correct, the amendatory paper will be amended in the examining group and notation made on the margin by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the next Office action the applicant should be informed of this alteration and of nonentry where defective directions and context leave doubt as to applicant's intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendatory clause is to be amended, it should be wholly rewritten and the original insertion canceled so that no interlineations or deletions shall appear in the clause as finally presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matter canceled by amendment can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the canceled matter as a new insertion. However, small amendments to a previous amendment that can be made easily without causing obscurity may be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decorum and discourtesy (37 CFR 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys or agents are required to conduct their business with the Patent and Trademark Office with decorum and courtesy. Papers presented in violation of this requirement will be submitted to the Commissioner and will be returned by his direct order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints against examiners must be made in communications separate from other papers. Technical support staff should briefly review papers before entry to determine whether discourteous remarks appear. If discourteous remarks appear, either ignore or submit the paper to the Group Director for possible return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and basic content required for 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit or declaration is to overcome a prior art rejection by proving invention of the claimed subject matter by applicant prior to the effective date of the reference relied upon in the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit or declaration must include facts showing a completion of the invention in this country or in a NAFTA or WTO member country before the filing date of the application on which the U.S. patent issued, or before the date of the foreign patent, or before the date of the printed publication. Original exhibits of drawings or records, or photocopies, must accompany and form part of the affidavit or declaration or their absence satisfactorily explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted situations for use of 37 CFR 1.131
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 may be used where (A) the date of the foreign patent or publication is less than 1 year prior to applicant’s effective filing date, and (B) where the reference is a U.S. patent with a patent date less than 1 year prior to applicant’s effective filing date that shows but does not claim the same patentable invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.131 is designed to permit applicant to overcome rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and (e) based on patents and publications which are not statutory bars but which have dates prior to the applicant's effective filing date yet subsequent to applicant's actual date of invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 37 CFR 1.131 is inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate in many situations, including: (A) reference publication date more than 1 year prior (statutory bar 35 U.S.C. 102(b)); (B) reference U.S. patent claims the same patentable invention; (C) reference is a foreign patent to applicant issued prior to domestic filing from an application filed >12 months earlier (35 U.S.C. 102(d)); (D) applicant's parent/PCT effective filing date is prior to the reference date; (E) prior U.S. patent to same entity claiming same invention (double patenting); (F) disclosure of prior U.S. patent to same party not copending (dedication); (G) applicant has clearly admitted subject matter is prior art; (H) subject matter is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(f); (I) subject matter is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(g); (J) lost count in an interference where doctrines bar use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cited MPEP sections and case law for specifics; 37 CFR 1.131 cannot overcome statutory bars or some 102(g) situations because those establish actual prior invention by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference effective date to be overcome
rubrics_metrics.description: The date to be overcome under 37 CFR 1.131 is the effective date of the reference (i.e., the date on which the reference is available as prior art). For U.S. patents this is the effective U.S. filing date (not foreign filing date); for printed publications it is the publication date; for foreign patents see MPEP §§ 2126–2127.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the portion of a patent relied on was introduced by amendment as new matter, the date to be overcome may be the date of amendment. Special rules apply for patents entitled to priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 35 U.S.C. 120/PCT national stage conversions; see MPEP for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for 37 CFR 1.131 responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.57–7.64 may be used to respond to 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits, including standard paragraphs identifying affidavits as ineffective or effective and stating specific deficiencies (e.g., insufficient reduction to practice, conception, diligence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using these form paragraphs, insert the appropriate bracketed information and follow preceding paragraph sequencing requirements (e.g., many must be preceded by paragraph 7.57).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific evidentiary requirements and common insufficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The showing of facts in a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration must be such, in character and weight, as to establish reduction to practice prior to the effective date of the reference, or conception prior to the reference coupled with due diligence from prior to said date to a subsequent reduction to practice or to filing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original exhibits or photocopies must accompany the affidavit or their absence satisfactorily explained. Common insufficiencies are: lack of evidence of reduction to practice (¶7.59), insufficient evidence of conception (¶7.61), lack of diligence (¶7.62), and insufficient evidence of actual reduction to practice (¶7.63). Each insufficiency paragraph should be used as required and accompanied by explanatory bracketed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.131 vs 37 CFR 1.132 — when each is appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations are for proving applicant's invention date to overcome prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (e). 37 CFR 1.132 affidavits/declarations are used where applicant can show that the subject matter relied upon in the reference was applicant's own invention (e.g., common ownership or derivation issues) or to traverse other specific grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits improperly filed under 1.131 when 1.132 is appropriate will be considered as though filed under 1.132. See MPEP § 716.10 for 1.132 practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint patent, common assignee, and coauthorship considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject matter disclosed (but not claimed) in a patent issued jointly to S and another is claimed later by S, the joint patent is a valid reference unless overcome by 1.131 or an unequivocal 1.132 declaration by S that he/she conceived the subject matter. Common assignee status alone does not avoid the need for 1.131 unless 1.132 shows derivation/ownership circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coauthors may overcome a rejection by filing a 1.131 affidavit or alternatively a 1.132 affidavit showing the article describes applicant's own work. Disclaimer by the other patentee is not required but may be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: How much of the claimed invention must be shown
rubrics_metrics.description: The 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit or declaration must establish possession of either the whole invention claimed or something falling within the claim (such as a species of a claimed genus), in the sense that the claim as a whole reads on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit need not show identical disclosure of the reference; it is sufficient if it shows completion commensurate with the extent of the invention as claimed in the reference. Where differences are small and treated by the examiner as obvious, an affidavit may be sufficient even if it does not show the particular feature, provided it establishes the basic inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swearing behind one of a plurality of combined references
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may overcome a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection based on a combination of references by showing completion of the invention by applicant prior to the effective date of any of the references; applicant need not antedate the earliest filing date among the combined references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the affidavit must still establish possession of the claimed invention (not merely what a reference happens to show), and may rely on teachings of a secondary reference to show differences would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill prior to the relevant reference date.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule as to generic claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference applied against generic claims may (in most cases) be antedated as to such claims by an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 showing completion of the invention of only a single species, within the genus, prior to the effective date of the reference (assuming the reference is not a statutory bar or a patent claiming the same invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule has exceptions (e.g., unpredictable arts) and case law nuances; see cited cases (Ex parte Biesecker; In re Fong; In re Defano) and MPEP § 715.03 for guidance in unpredictable arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-species / unpredictable arts practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Where generic claims have been rejected on a reference that discloses a species not antedated by the affidavit, the rejection will not ordinarily be withdrawn unless the applicant can establish possession of the genus or that predictability permits antedating from a single species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules apply in unpredictable arts; applicant must establish possession of the claimed genus or other showing sufficient under case law and MPEP guidance.
